hints: Start by remembering what the Contact process is made for, and whether its aqueous product is acidic or basic.
An acid is neutralised by a base, so think about which common gas acts as a base in water.
Now ask which of the four listed processes actually makes that basic gas on a large scale.
walkthrough:
**Identify Z from the Contact process**

The Contact process oxidises sulfur to make sulfur trioxide, which is then converted to concentrated sulfuric acid. So Z is $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

$$2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3 \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$

**Decide what type of gas is needed**

An aqueous solution of Z is strongly acidic. To neutralise an acid you need a base.

The only common gas that is basic and forms $\text{OH}^-$ in water is ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$:
$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-$$

**Match ammonia to its manufacturing process**

Ammonia is manufactured on a large scale by the Haber process from nitrogen and hydrogen.

$$\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$$

That basic gas will then neutralise sulfuric acid, for example to make ammonium sulfate fertiliser.

options.A: Atmospheric lightning provides enough energy for $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ to react to form nitrogen oxides such as $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$. These dissolve to give acidic solutions, so they would add acidity, not neutralise the sulfuric acid.
options.B: High temperature combustion in an engine also produces nitrogen oxides ($\text{NO}_x$) plus $\text{CO}_2$. Both are acidic oxides. They cannot neutralise an acid, this is a classic acid rain trap.
options.C: The Haber process makes ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, which is a basic gas. It reacts with water to give $\text{OH}^-$ and neutralises $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form ammonium salts such as $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$.
options.D: Thermal decomposition of a Group 2 nitrate, e.g. $2\text{Mg}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$, gives nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. $\text{NO}_2$ is an acidic gas and forms nitric acid in water, so it will not neutralise sulfuric acid.
